group.passage: Today, almost everyone knows that washing our hands helps stop the spread of disease. Less than two hundred years ago, however, many doctors did not believe this. The story of Ignaz Semmelweis, a Hungarian doctor, shows how hard it can be to change an old habit, even when the facts are clear. In the 1840s, Semmelweis worked at the Vienna General Hospital in Austria. The hospital had two wards where women gave birth. One was run by male doctors and medical students, and the other by female midwives. Semmelweis noticed something terrible: women in the doctors' ward were dying of a disease called childbed fever at more than twice the rate of those cared for by midwives. He also learned that the doctors and students often came to the ward right after examining dead bodies, while the midwives never did this kind of work. In 1847, Semmelweis made handwashing a rule for every doctor and student in his ward. Instead of plain soap, he used a cleaning liquid made with chlorine, because it took away the smell of death from their hands. Soon, the number of mothers who died fell sharply. Sadly, his message fell on deaf ears: most doctors in Vienna refused to accept it. Historians believe that some of them did not like the idea that doctors were causing their own patients' deaths. The hospital even stopped the handwashing rule, and Semmelweis died in 1865 without seeing his ideas accepted. Two years later, a surgeon named Joseph Lister began to call for cleaning both hands and tools, and by the 1870s, surgeons regularly washed before operations. Today, a university in Budapest is named after Semmelweis, and October 15 is Global Handwashing Day. Studies show that washing hands with soap can prevent about 1 in 3 cases of diarrhea and 1 in 5 infections of the nose, throat, and lungs.

translation_zh.text:
今天幾乎每個人都知道，洗手有助於阻止疾病傳播。然而不到兩百年前，許多醫生並不相信這件事。匈牙利醫生伊格納茲・塞麥爾維斯的故事說明了，即使事實很清楚，要改變一個舊習慣仍然可能非常困難。
1840 年代，塞麥爾維斯在奧地利的維也納總醫院工作。這家醫院有兩個產婦分娩的病房。一個由男醫生和醫學生負責，另一個由女助產士負責。塞麥爾維斯注意到一件可怕的事：在醫生病房的婦女死於一種叫做產褥熱的疾病，死亡率是助產士照顧的婦女的兩倍以上。他也得知，醫生和學生常常剛檢查完遺體就直接到病房，而助產士從來不做這類工作。
1847 年，塞麥爾維斯規定他病房裡的每位醫生和學生都要洗手。他不用普通肥皂，而用一種含氯的清潔液，因為它能去除他們手上的死亡氣味。很快地，死亡的產婦人數大幅下降。
可惜的是，他的話沒有人聽：維也納大多數醫生拒絕接受。歷史學家認為，有些醫生不喜歡「醫生自己造成病人死亡」這種想法。醫院甚至停止了洗手的規定，塞麥爾維斯在 1865 年過世，沒能看到自己的想法被接受。兩年後，一位名叫約瑟夫・李斯特的外科醫生開始呼籲把手和工具都清潔乾淨；到了 1870 年代，外科醫生在手術前洗手已經成為常規。今天，布達佩斯有一所大學以塞麥爾維斯命名，而 10 月 15 日是全球洗手日。研究顯示，用肥皂洗手可以預防大約三分之一的腹瀉，以及五分之一的鼻、喉和肺部感染。

checked.claim: Less than two hundred years ago many doctors did not believe handwashing stops disease.（1847 年至今約 179 年）
Ignaz Semmelweis, a Hungarian doctor, worked at the Vienna General Hospital in Austria in the 1840s.（f1；National Geographic 原頁 2026-10-09 複查一致）
The hospital had two wards where women gave birth, one run by male doctors and medical students, the other by female midwives.（f2）
Women in the doctors' ward died of childbed fever at more than twice the rate of those cared for by midwives.（f3；NG 原頁：more than twice the rate）
Doctors and students came to the ward right after examining dead bodies; the midwives never did this kind of work.（f4）
In 1847 Semmelweis made handwashing a rule for every doctor and student in his ward.（f5）
He used a cleaning liquid made with chlorine instead of plain soap because it took away the smell of death from their hands.（f6；NG 原頁：chlorinated lime solution…removed the smell of decay）
Soon, the number of mothers who died fell sharply.（f7）
Most doctors in Vienna refused to accept it; historians believe some disliked the idea that doctors were causing their patients' deaths.（f8）
The hospital stopped the handwashing rule, and Semmelweis died in 1865 without seeing his ideas accepted.（f9、f10）

Two years later Joseph Lister began to call for cleaning both hands and tools, and by the 1870s surgeons regularly washed before operations.（f11；NG 原頁：In 1867…in the 1870s physicians began regularly scrubbing up）
A university in Budapest is named after Semmelweis.（f12）
October 15 is Global Handwashing Day.（f13；CDC 原頁經 WebFetch 複查：Each year on October 15）

Washing hands with soap can prevent about 1 in 3 cases of diarrhea and 1 in 5 infections of the nose, throat, and lungs.（f14；CDC 原頁：1 in 3 diarrhea-related sicknesses、1 in 5 respiratory infections；鼻喉肺感染＝呼吸道感染）
